Chilean Gas & Water Utilities Workers Stage Walkout, Disrupting Core Operations

A nationwide strike by workers in Chile’s Gas & Water Utilities industry entered its second day on Tuesday, prompting widespread operational disruptions at plants, pipelines, and treatment facilities across the country. The walkout, organized by the National Federation of Gas & Water Employees (FENTAGUA), began early Monday after contract negotiations with major employers broke down over demands for improved wages and enhanced safety protocols.

At Aquasur, one of the industry’s leading firms, management confirmed that two of its water treatment plants in the Valparaíso region have reduced capacity by over 60% due to staff shortages. “We have activated contingency protocols, but these measures are limited,” said operations director Pablo Molina. “Our priority is to ensure the safety of remaining personnel and maintain essential functions where possible.”

Gasandes, a major natural gas distributor, reported that field maintenance operations have been suspended at its Santiago and Concepción facilities. “Routine inspections and minor repairs are on hold, and we are closely monitoring key infrastructure,” a company spokesperson said. The spokesperson added that the company is “ready to resume talks with union representatives at any time.”

Union officials said more than 4,500 workers from 18 companies have joined the walkout, affecting both urban and rural sites. “Our members are united in their demand for fair pay and safer working conditions. The companies have not addressed our concerns,” said FENTAGUA president Carla Riquelme at a press briefing in Santiago.

Industry analysts estimate that up to 70% of the country’s gas and water utility workforce has participated in the strike. “The longer the walkout continues, the greater the logistical and financial strain on the sector,” said Esteban Vilches, an independent utilities consultant. “Firms face mounting challenges in maintaining service levels and meeting regulatory compliance.”

As negotiations remain at a standstill, both union leaders and company officials have expressed willingness to return to the table. However, with no agreement in sight, the strike’s impact on Gas & Water Utilities operations is expected to intensify in the coming days.
